transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2028-12-05 10:00 AM ET
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Ross (CTO - Fjord), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Marco Silva (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Product), Sam (SRE)
Links shared: benchmark harness (https://drive.redwood.dev/fjord/bench-harness), security pack (https://redwood.docs/security/fjord-scan)

Summary:
- Fjord is exploring Redwood for a streaming-heavy product (real-time copiloting in a desktop app). Primary asks: p95 <= 250ms for short prompts, sustained token/sec during bursts (~5k tokens/sec cluster), graceful degrade on capacity, and an enterprise-grade security posture (SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS).
- We discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs and sketched a 2-week sandbox to run token/sec sims.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this. quick intro round robin?
[00:00:06] Evan Ross: Evan Ross, CTO at Fjord Systems. thanks, we are time boxed to 45 minutes, we have a couple of specific SLO questions.
[00:00:12] Priya Nair: priya, head of ML. i'll own the prompt set and metrics.
[00:00:17] Lucas Patel: lucas, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll run the perf side and help on the sandbox.
[00:00:22] Marco Silva: marco, infra. i'll ask a lot of timing questions.
[00:00:26] Lena Ortiz: lena, product - mostly here to understand user impact.

[00:01:05] Maya Chen: quick context from our side — Redwood supports hosted api, reserved dedicated pools, and private vpc or on-prem. for streaming use cases we typically recommend dedicated if you need predictable burst behavior and private if you need full network isolation and KMS controls. but we can baseline on hosted for the sandbox.
[00:01:34] Evan Ross: our main constraint is latency. we need p95 under 250ms for short completions (up to 80 tokens) and acceptable degraded performance for long streams. can you realistically hit that on hosted?
[00:01:46] Lucas Patel: short answer: yes for certain model sizes with optimized runtime and kv caching, but it depends on concurrency and tokenization patterns. have you measured current token/sec load?
[00:01:56] Priya Nair: right now our internal sim shows about 60 concurrent users at peak, each with interactive streams, that's roughly 3-4k tokens/sec sustained, spikes to ~6k for 30s during launches.
[00:02:10] Marco Silva: and we run this out of a eu-west region, data residency matters.

[00:02:35] Maya Chen: good — so two axes: p95 latency for short requests and throughput (token/sec) for bursts. for p95 under 250 we typically recommend pinning to a dedicated pool with smaller batch windows and prefix caching. hosted can hit it occasionally but with noisy neighbors the p95 may move, especially under bursty traffic.
[00:03:02] Evan Ross: noisy neighbors is our worry. we don't want to overprovision for base traffic. what's the typical quantization/throughput tradeoff you'd recommend?
[00:03:12] Lucas Patel: we use quantized variants for throughput — int8 or bfloat16 profiles can double token/sec but may slightly affect quality. Redwood Optimize can recommend profiles per workload, we can run an eval on your prompt set.

[00:03:40] [00:03:40] Priya Nair: how does streaming p95 measurement work in your console? we need traceability to user request ids, token-by-token timing.
[00:03:50] Maya Chen: console gives per-request token latency breakdown, p50/p95/p99, and you can trace by request id. we also capture token stream times and have hooks for span-level tracing to tie into your tracing system. there's an example in the docs but sometimes the transcription churns 'span' to 'spin' in the docs — apologies for that.

[00:04:22] Marco Silva: security question — we are SOC2 compliant and require SSO/SAML, RBAC, and customer-managed KMS for private. does Redwood support HSM backends or bring-your-own-key?
[00:04:33] Lucas Patel: yes to KMS integrations, we support cloud KMS providers and HSM in Private deployment. for Hosted we offer envelope encryption — we can discuss enterprise KMS for Dedicated/Private. I'll drop the security pack link after the call.

[00:05:01] Evan Ross: ok, walk me through a sample benchmark you'd run for us.
[00:05:06] Maya Chen: hypoth — we run three phases: 1) small-sample latency profile using your 10-20 canonical prompts (measure p95 for <80 tokens), 2) steady-state throughput with concurrency matching your baseline (simulate 60 users), 3) burst reproducibility with 30-60s high token/sec spikes to see p95 shifts and tail behavior.
[00:05:30] Priya Nair: what do you need from us to start?
[00:05:34] Lucas Patel: prompt set, tokenization examples, and a traffic trace for an hour if possible. if not, we can synthesize traffic but real traces are best. also region preference and whether private networking is required.

[00:06:05] Lena Ortiz: and UX-wise, if streaming degrades we need a graceful fallback — maybe a smaller model or cached prefix. can Redwood do automatic fallback?
[00:06:15] Maya Chen: yes, routing policies can fallback to cheaper variants or to dedicated fallback pools. we can also configure canary deploy rules so you won't see a sudden change.

[00:06:45] [00:06:45] Marco Silva: i'd like specific numbers — for example if we run a 4-GPU dedicated pool, what sustained tokens/sec could we expect for a 13B model at int8?
[00:06:56] Lucas Patel: rough back-of-envelope: for a 13B quantized profile on A100-ish hardware, you might see ~800-1200 tokens/sec per GPU depending on sequence length and decode strategy, so 4 GPUs could be around 3.2k-4.8k tokens/sec sustained; with optimizations and batching you can push bursts higher. those numbers vary a lot with beam/temperature and streaming chunk sizes.

[00:07:38] Evan Ross: so to hit our spikes to 6k tokens/sec for 30 seconds we'd need either larger GPU pool or autoscaling/burst capacity?
[00:07:45] Lucas Patel: correct — autoscaling with a burst reserve or a hybrid of dedicated + hosted fallback allows you to keep base cost down and still handle spikes. Redwood Dedicated supports configurable burst capacity to hosted nodes if you allow fallback.

[00:08:06] Priya Nair: can the fallback preserve request consistency? we can't have different completions between models.
[00:08:14] Maya Chen: that's a common concern — we recommend model variants that are architecturally compatible (same tokenizer and same family) to minimize regressions; we also run quality guards and regressions tests against a held-out eval set before enabling fallback.

[00:08:39] [00:08:39] Sam (SRE): latency SLO enforcement question: if p95 breaches, can we auto-throttle or shed load?
[00:08:46] Lucas Patel: yes, Redwood Console supports automatic throttling policies and circuit breakers per-route or per-account. you can set token-level throttles and automatic fallbacks.

[00:09:12] Lena Ortiz: from product perspective, is streaming partial tokens counted differently for billing? we need to map budgets to features.
[00:09:20] Maya Chen: billing is token-based; streaming doesn't double count, but we provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console so you can attribute cost to features and tokens.

[00:09:48] Evan Ross: let's dig into the sandbox plan — we want to run a baseline latency run on hosted then a dedicated pass, then a private pass if we decide. timeline?
[00:09:58] Lucas Patel: 2-week sandbox is typical: week 1 baseline hosted + config tuning, week 2 dedicated sizing and burst tests. if private needed, that's parallel but requires networking and KMS setup ~2-3 more weeks.

[00:10:23] Priya Nair: for the hosted baseline what model families do you recommend? lightweight for interactive — 7B/13B?
[00:10:31] Lucas Patel: yes 7B for very low-latency interactive, 13B for better quality at slightly higher per-token cost. for streaming the decode latency matters, so 7B with int8 might give your p95 targets easiest.

[00:10:55] [00:10:55] Marco Silva: a bit skeptical — we need real numbers, not marketing. can you run a pilot with our prompts and send the resulting p95 scatter?
[00:11:03] Maya Chen: absolutely, that's part of the action items. we'll need the prompt set and a trace. Lucas will run the harness.

[00:11:22] Evan Ross: region/residency — we need EU data to stay in eu-west. hosted supports that?
[00:11:28] Maya Chen: yes we have eu-west hosted regions and dedicated pools can be provisioned there. private deployments of course give you full control.

[00:11:45] Priya Nair: are there any tradeoffs with using a smaller context window to save latency? some of our prompts use 2-3k tokens context.
[00:11:53] Lucas Patel: long contexts increase KV cache and memory footprint, which raises per-request latency; we can recommend offloading older context or using summarization to reduce active context length. for p95 interactive flows we optimize for short working contexts.

[00:12:20] [00:12:20] Priya Nair: in your previous notes i remember 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K V catch' — how robust is the runtime to reusing kvcache across short sessions?
[00:12:30] Lucas Patel: it's robust — continuous batching and KV reuse reduce compute by up to 30% for repeated prefixes. it's one of the levers we'll tune in the sandbox.

[00:12:55] Marco Silva: okay, security again — we need logs for external audit and immutable audit trail, can Redwood stream logs to our S3?
[00:13:03] Maya Chen: yes, audit logs and request traces can be pushed to your storage. for Private we can also enable internal syslogs/HSM audit hooks.

[00:13:30] Evan Ross: chaos scenario — if a node fails mid-burst, what's the expected user visible impact?
[00:13:38] Lucas Patel: autoscaling and graceful degradation minimize user impact; for streaming we keep partial progress and can fallback to a smaller model. worst case you'd see longer tail but not complete outage if fallback paths are enabled.

[00:14:05] [00:14:05] Lena Ortiz: do you have examples of customers using Redwood for similar live copilots?
[00:14:11] Maya Chen: yes, we have several—i can share anonymized case studies. i'll include the link in follow-up.

[00:14:30] Marco Silva: about costs — can you ballpark a monthly cost for baseline 60 concurrent users with bursts to 6k tokens/sec on dedicated?
[00:14:38] Maya Chen: rough estimate depends on model and GPU type; for 13B quantized on A100 equivalent, ballpark for reserved capacity could be in the low-to-mid five figures monthly for a modest pool, bursts add variable charges. we'll produce a more precise cost estimate after the sandbox test.

[00:15:05] [00:15:05] Priya Nair: sample artifacts — Priya: i'll upload prompt set to the shared drive tonight.
[00:15:11] Maya Chen: great — action item noted. Lucas will also post the benchmark harness link.

[00:15:30] Marco Silva: one more — compliance: we need SOC2 attestation and penetration test reports. do you have those available?
[00:15:38] Lucas Patel: yes, SOC2 Type II, pen test summaries are in the security pack link i'll share. full reports available under NDA.

[00:16:00] Evan Ross: ok, let's summarize next steps and owners.
[00:16:05] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to provision a hosted sandbox and share the benchmark harness (Maya), customer to upload prompt set and 1-hour trace (Priya), Redwood SE to run baseline hosted tests and then dedicated sizing (Lucas), follow-up call after initial sandbox run to review p95/tail and cost.
[00:16:30] Priya Nair: timeline — can we get the hosted baseline results within 5 business days?
[00:16:35] Lucas Patel: yes that's doable if we get traces and prompts by EOD tomorrow.

[00:16:52] [00:16:52] Sam (SRE): quick ops nit — access: for sandbox do you provision API keys per-user or a single test key? we want to instrument per-user metrics.
[00:17:00] Maya Chen: we can provision per-user tokens and instrument request-level metadata to map back to your ids.

[00:17:20] Lena Ortiz: question about model regressions — do you do A/B comparisons during rollout?
[00:17:25] Lucas Patel: yes, rollout features allow canarying small percentages, A/Bs, and automated rollback on quality regressions against your eval set.

[00:17:48] Evan Ross: competitors — we've talked to Anthropic and a managed OpenAI partner. what makes Redwood different?
[00:17:56] Maya Chen: our production-first runtime, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and cost/perf tooling — plus rollout and fallback primitives aimed at real-time apps.

[00:18:15] [00:18:15] Priya Nair: any gotchas you want us to watch for in prompt set prep? we have long few-shot prompts.
[00:18:23] Lucas Patel: keep the live context minimal or move examples into a retrieval layer; few-shot examples multiply token cost and increase latency. we'll show techniques in the sandbox.

[00:18:50] Marco Silva: can we get token-level traces back to our tracing destination? we need to correlate to our Jaeger spans.
[00:18:58] Maya Chen: yes, tracing hooks available — we map request ids to spans and can push to your traces.

[00:19:20] [00:19:20] Evan Ross: ok final check: can you deliver the baseline report and cost estimate by next thursday?
[00:19:27] Lucas Patel: yes, assuming we get artifacts today or tomorrow.

[00:19:45] Maya Chen: great — i'll send the follow-up email and next steps. i'll also attach the security pack and the bench harness link.
[00:19:55] Priya Nair: thanks all. one more micro question — for streaming p95 calculation do you measure from first token or from request start?
[00:20:03] Lucas Patel: both: console shows first-byte latency and last-token latency; you can choose the metric for SLO.

[00:20:25] [00:20:25] Lena Ortiz: thanks, that's helpful.
[00:20:30] Evan Ross: good session. we'll upload assets tonight. talk soon.

[00:20:38] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, talk soon—end of call.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-transcribed technical terms ("K V catch" for KV cache, "sam-el" for SAML), and speaker overlaps with short crosstalk.
